Samir here. Last term Bidisha showed me her note-taking method, and my own notes were a mess, so I said I'd try it for one week. Only one.
The method has three parts: a summary box at the top of each page, colour codes for definitions, examples and doubts, and a margin for questions. On the first day the summary box made me stop and say the lecture in two lines, which showed me at once what I hadn't understood. The colour codes were another matter. Swapping pens took so long that I lost the lecturer's next sentence twice.
After a week I kept the box and the margin and dropped the colours. I told Bidisha the box was her best idea and the pens my worst habit.

qa.a: The method has a summary box at the top of each page, colour codes for definitions, examples and doubts, and a margin for questions.

qa.q: What did Samir feel about the colour codes?
qa.a: Samir felt frustrated with them, since swapping pens took so long that the lecturer's next sentence was lost twice.

qa.q: What could Samir do to test another borrowed method?
qa.a: Samir could again try it for a short week and keep only the parts that help, since the summary box fit and the colour codes did not.

qa.q: How might Bidisha feel when hearing that only some of the method was kept?
qa.a: Bidisha may feel pleased that the summary box helped, and not offended, since Samir called it her best idea.

grounding: A student tries a friend's note-taking method for a week, keeps the summary box and drops the slowing colour codes.

Academic mentor's note: Sachin, first year, week 6

Sachin came to me worried that his notes were a mess. His friend Lalremsiami had shown him her method: colour codes for definitions, examples and questions, plus a summary box at the bottom of each page. Instead of switching everything at once, Sachin tried it for one week, only in chemistry. Today he showed me the results. He said the colour codes slowed him down; he spent more time choosing pens than listening. But the summary box helped a lot. Writing three lines at the end of each lecture made him notice what he hadn't understood. So he has dropped the colours and kept the box, now in all his subjects. I suggested he look back at his summary boxes before each weekly quiz.

qa.q: For how long did Sachin try the new method?
How did Sachin feel about the colour codes?
qa.a: He felt frustrated with them, because choosing pens slowed him down and pulled attention from the lecture.

qa.q: Why was trying the method on one subject first a good idea?
qa.a: It let Sachin test what fitted him without risking all his notes, so he kept the helpful summary box and dropped the rest.

qa.q: How might Lalremsiami see Sachin keeping only part of her method?
qa.a: She might feel pleased that the summary box helped, and understand that the colours suit her more than him.

grounding: A student tries a friend's note-taking method for a week, keeps the summary box and drops the colour codes that slow him down.

Sunday

One week of Tenzin's note method, done. Tenzin swears by it: three colours of pen, a symbol for every type of point, and a summary box at the end of each lecture. Here's my honest review, for myself. Colours: no. I spent half the physics lecture switching pens and missed the derivation. Symbols: I forgot what the triangle meant by Wednesday. But the summary box? Yes. Writing three lines at the end of each class made me notice what I didn't get, and I asked two questions on Thursday that I'd never have asked before. So I'm keeping the box, dropping the rest. One pen, one box. Farhan, you're allowed to borrow half an idea, beta, as Ammi says.

qa.q: What did Farhan miss while switching pens?
qa.a: The derivation, in half the physics lecture.

qa.q: How does Farhan feel about the summary box?
qa.a: Farhan feels pleased and more confident, since it helped notice gaps and ask two questions.

qa.q: Which approach suits Farhan better than copying Tenzin fully?
qa.a: Keeping only the part that works, the summary box, and dropping colours and symbols that slowed things down.

qa.q: How might Tenzin see Farhan's review?
qa.a: Tenzin might feel a bit surprised the colours were dropped, but glad the summary box was useful.

grounding: A student tests a friend's note-taking method for a week, keeps the summary box and drops the colour codes that slow things down.
